Use of Alkali Activated Concrete for 
Precast Products — Guidelines 


ICS 91.100

Cement Matrix Products Sectional Committee, CED 53 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Cement 
Matrix Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


The advancements in material sciences have led to development of altogether alternative binding material to 
concrete in the form of alkali activated concrete or geopolymer concrete (which is considered part of broad group 
of alkali activated materials). Alkali activated concrete are a relatively newer class of building material. Owing to 
increased environmental concerns as well as diminishing natural resources alkali activated concrete are spotted as 
a valuable alternative for Portland cement. Alkali activated concrete can have similar cementing characteristics as 
Portland cement, but they can be produced out of by-products from other industry (for example, fly ash) or less 
energy craving and CO, emitting materials (for example, calcined clay) using alkali activators. 


The study of the alkali activation process of aluminosilicate sources (for example, fly ash and calcined clay) 
as a method of synthesizing new cementitious materials is gaining relevance in the scientific community. The 
increasing number of scientific publications as well as international events dedicated to this topic is proof of it. 
Currently, there are, however, not many practical applications. 


The alternative works out to be green and sustainable but there are apprehensions regarding costs, testing methods 
and field performance. 


A lot of research is being carried out nationally and internationally. Based on researches conducted, it is apt time 
to have standard guidelines relating to production and use of geopolymer concrete as a potential supplement/ 
compliment to hydraulic cement concrete. 


In the formulation of this standard, assistance has been drawn from Austroads Specifications, SINTEF 
report on geopolymers, RILEM state-of-the-art report on alkali activated materials, geopolymer 
(chemistry and applications) by Joseph Davidovits, and the extensive experimental work carried out by the 
National Council for Cement and Building Materials, India. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17452 : 2020 


Indian Standard 


USE OF ALKALI ACTIVATED CONCRETE FOR 
PRECAST PRODUCTS — GUIDELINES 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies constituent materials, mix 
design procedure, curing requirements, for solid, 
unreinforced precast alkali activated concrete. 
The potential applications can be paver blocks, 
kerb stones, blocks, etc. The grades shall be limited 
up to M 40. 


1.2 The precast products produced using alkali 
activated concrete as per this standard shall not be 
used for structural applications without satisfactory 
data regarding safety and results of testing for required 
strength parameters. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated in Annex A. 


3 DEFINITIONS 


For the purpose of this standard the definition given 
below shall apply. 


3.1 Alkali Activated Materials 


Alkali activation is a generic term which is 
applied to the reaction of a solid aluminosilicate 
(termed the ‘precursor’) under alkaline conditions 
(induced by the ‘alkali activator’), to produce a 
hardened binder which is based on a combination of 
hydrous alkali-aluminosilicate and/or alkali-alkali 
earth-aluminosilicate phases. Additional terminology 
which is often used with regard to these materials can 
include ‘geopolymer’ nomenclature which is used to 
describe low-calcium alkali-activated aluminosilicate 
binders. In geopolymers the pseudo-zeolitic network 
structure is formed rather than chain characteristic of 
calcium sillicate hydrates. 


4 MATERIALS 


4.1 Binding Materials 


The binding materials used for preparation of alkali 
activated concrete shall include any one or more of the 
following: 


a) Pulverized fuel ash conforming to IS 3812 
(Part 1). 


b) Ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) 
conforming to IS 16714. 

c) Metakaolin conforming to IS 16354. 

d) Calcined clay conforming to IS 1344. 

e) Silica fume conforming to IS 15388. 


NOTE — The widely accepted practices have been of utilizing 
a combination of GGBFS and fly ash for producing alkali 
activated concrete. 


4.2 Alkali Activators 


The activators used for preparation of alkali activated 
concrete shall include any one or more of the following: 


a) Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) conforming to IS 252. 


b) Potassium hydroxide (KOH) conforming to 
IS 6831. 


c) Sodium silicate (alkaline grade) conforming to 
IS 381. 


d) Potassium silicate conforming to IS 8813. 
e) Sodium carbonate conforming to IS 251. 
f) Potassium carbonate conforming to IS 7129. 


NOTE — The most commonly used activators are sodium 
hydroxide, sodium sillicate, combination of sodium sillicate 
and sodium hydroxide, combination of potassium silicate and 
potassium hydroxide. It is pertinent to mention that for sodium 
silicates alkaline grade of activators are required. 


4.3 Admixtures 


The admixtures to be employed for usage in making 
alkali activated concrete can be any one of the 
following: 


a) Sulphonated napthalene formaldehyde, 
sulphonated melamine formaldehyde and 
lignosulphonates based chemical admixtures. 


b) Sucrose. 


c) Any other compatible admixture, such as organic 
acids like diluted tartaric acid, citric acid, etc. 
However, no detrimental effect shall be observed 
on the concrete. It is pertinent to mention that 
not only the admixtures but the role of binding 
materials and activators is more pronounced in 
controlling workability. 


4.4 Coarse Aggregates 


Coarse aggregates shall conform to the requirements of 
IS 383. 


IS 17452 : 2020 


4.5 Fine Aggregates 


Fine aggregates shall conform to the requirements of 
IS 383. 


4.6 Water 


The water used in production of concrete shall conform 
to the requirements specified in IS 456. 


4.7 Preferred Composition 


The following guidelines can be adopted for the mix 
design: 


a) Dry binding material shall not be less than 
280 kg/m’. The composition should include 
reactive SiO, between 15 to 40 percent by weight 
of total binding material and the preferable ratio 
of reactive SiO,/Al,O, by mass in dry binding 
material is 2.5 to 4. 

NOTES 

1 The dry binding material doesn’t include any contribution 
from activators or activating solutions. The preferred chemical 
composition of dry binding material can be achieved by using 
two or more binding materials from the list given in 4.1. This 
can be achieved by mixing different binders in ratios by trial 
and error (for example, trying GGBF : fly ash : 30 : 70 by mass 
and checking chemical composition of mix using individual 
values of mix) so as to achieve the chemical composition of 
final mix as given above. 

2 Procedures for reactive SiO, and Al,O, determination may be 
referred from IS 3812 (Part 1) and IS 1727 respectively. 

The Na,O percent in the activator solution added 
to the mix shall not be less than 5 percent of dry 
binding material by mass. 

c) The activator modulus (SiO,/Na,O by mass) 
should preferably be kept less than 2 and greater 
than 0.6. 

The total water to dry binding material ratio by 
mass shall be kept less than 0.60. 


NOTE — The total water in the mix means total water in the 


b 


wm 


d 


— 


mix that is, water already present in activators and water added 
to the mix. Some activators like sodium hydroxide, sodium 
sillicate gel have some water already present. The same water 
is counted as water from activators. Added water is total water 
in the mix required (based on water to dry binding material) 
minus water present in the activators. 


5 MIX DESIGN 


5.1 The design for 1 m? concrete mix 
(for mixes workable up to 30 min) shall be carried out 


step-wise as given below: 

a) Step 1: Selection of Target Compressive Strength 
Target compressive strength = (f, + 10 MPa). 
Higher value may be adopted, if required keeping in 
view the variations in standard deviations in mixes. 
For lower grades a lower value may be adopted. 


Step 2: Selection of Binder Content and Water 
Binder Ratio (Based on MSA 20 mm) 

The typical ratios are given below. For 
intermediate grades, the values can be interpolated. 


b 


= 


SI Target Minimum Maximum 

No. Compressive Binder Total 

Strength Material Water-Binder 

MPa Content (Dry) Material Ratio 

(1) (2) (3) (4) 

i) 10 Mpa 280 0.60 
11) 20 MPa 320 0.50 
111) 30 MPa 350 0.45 
iv) 40 MPa 400 0.40 


The reactive SiO,/Al,O, ratio by weight of dry binding 
material should be broadly in range given in 4.7. 


c) Step 3: Selection of Dosage of Activator 


1) The Na,O percent shall preferably be kept 
as 5 to 10 percent of dry binder material (by 
weight). In cases when desired compressive 
strength is not achieved then this dosage may 
be increased. 


2) The activator modulus of solution 
(SiO,/Na,0) should preferably be kept 
between 0.6 to 2. As a guiding principle, 
usually the mixes containing more fly ash 
generally require lesser activator modulus and 
mixes containing more GGBFS require higher 
activator modulus.

wa 


Calculate total SiO, required based on selected 
activator modulus and Na,O percent selected. 


4 


a 


Calculate dosage of sodium (or potassium) 
sillicate required based on SiO, required from 
activator. The composition of sodium sillicate 
is critical here. The grade of sodium sillicate 
should preferably be alkaline and in gel form. 
For example, commonly available commercial 
sodium sillicate gel usually has a composition: 
SiO, = 30 to 35 percent, Na,O = 12 to 18 
percent, H,O = 40 to 50 percent). However, for 
calculations purpose, exact amount is required. 
5) Based on the calculated amount of sodium 
sillicate gel, calculate Na,O in kg contributed 
by the gel. Based on this calculation, calculate 
remaining Na,O (in kg) required (from total 
Na,O percent selected in first point of the step). 
6) The remaining Na,O (in kg) has to come 
through NaOH taken. 
Calculate NaOH (in kg) based on remaining 
Na,O required (in kg). (1 g NaOH = 0.775 g 
Na,O + 0.225 g H,O) 
d) Step 4: Preparation of Activator Solution 
1) Take total amount of NaOH (in kg) required 
for mix in a container of suitable size. 


7 


— 


2) Take an amount of water equal to 3 to 4 times 
by mass of total NaOH taken in a separate 
container (this amount is to be deducted from 
total water required for the mix). 


3) Mix the total NaOH taken and water taken 
as calculated in previous step preferably 
12 h to 24 h before casting. This is done to 
dissipate heat (being safety concern) and to get 
volume of solution stabilized. 

4) Mix the calculated amount of sodium silicate 
gel in the prepared solution (as prepared in 
previous steps) 3 to 5 h before casting. 

NOTES 

1 For larger amount of dissolution of NaOH additional water 

may be added to the mix to account for evaporation losses and 

solutions must be prepared in covered containers. 

2 Suitable safety precautions shall be taken while handling of 

chemicals and solutions. 


e) Step 5: Calculating Remaining Water for the Mix 


<~ 


Remaining water = Total water required from 
total water to binding materials ratio — water 
from sodium sillicate gel — water from sodium 
hydroxide — water already mixed to prepare 
solution of sodium hydroxide. 


f) Step 6: Calculation of Total Aggregate Quantity 


1) Total aggregate quantity required 
(volume in m?) (using say two binders, 
Binder 1 and Binder 2 weighed in kg) 
= 1 — {(Binder 1/sp. gr. of Binder 1 x 1 000) + 
(Binder 2/sp. gr. of Binder 2 x 1 000) + 
(Remaining water required / 1 x 1 000) + 
(Sodium sillicate gel/sp. gr. of sod. silicate 
x 1 000) + (NaOH solution/sp. gr. NaOH 
solution x 1 000)} 


NOTE — The adjustments for air content may also be taken in 


account as per IS 10262 for more accurate calculations. 

2) The specific gravity of NaOH solution prepared 
shall be determined exactly or in case not 
possible may be assumed between 1.24 to 1.30. 


a 


Step 7: Selection of Percentage Fine Aggregate 

and Calculation of Fine Aggregate Quantity 

1) The fine aggregate should be as per IS 10262. 
The exact percentage shall be arrived by 
experience and workability and cohesiveness 
of the mix. 


8 


2 


— 


Calculate fine aggregate in kg as: 


Fine aggregate = (selected fine aggregate 
percent/100) x total aggregate volume in m? x 
density in kg/m? x 1 000 


h) Step 8: Calculation of Coarse Aggregate 


The remaining quantity of aggregate shall be the coarse 
aggregate and can be calculated in similar procedure as 
given in previous step. 


Example: 


Problem Statement — Mix: M 30, fly ash: GGBFS in 
binder = 70 : 30 (arrived based on 4.7) 


Solution: 
Step 1: Selection of Target Compressive Strength 
Target compressive strength = 30 + 10 = 40 Mpa 


IS 17452 : 2020 


Step 2: Selection Content and 


Water-Binder Ratio 


of Binder 


Binder content = 400 kg, water-binder ratio = 0.45, 
Fly ash = 0.7 x 400 = 280 kg, GGBFS = 0.3 x 400 = 
120 kg 
Step 3: Selection of Dosage of Activator 
a) Na,O percent = 8 percent of dry binder material 
(by mass) = 8 x 400/100 = 32 kg 
b) Taking activator modulus of solution SiO,/Na,O 
=1.5 
c) Total SiO, required based on selected activator 
modulus = 1.5 x 32 = 48 kg 


d) Dosage of sodium sillicate = 48/0.33 = 145 kg 
Assumed composition of sodium Sillicate gel 
is: SiO, percent = 33 percent, Na,O percent = 
15 percent, H,O = 52 percent 


Na,O in kg coming from the gel = 0.15 x 145 
= 22 kg 


f) Remaining Na,O in kg required = 32 —22 = 10 kg 
g) NaOH in kg = 10/0.775 = 13kg 


Step 4: Preparation of activator solution 


e 


wm 


Prepare solution of NaOH. The volume of solution 
may be taken equal to water added. In this case, the 
water added shall be 13 kg x 3 = 39 litre 


Step 5: Calculation of Remaining Water for the Mix 


Remaining water = 0.40 x 400 — 145 x 0.52 — 
13 x 0.225 - 39 = 162 — 75 — 2.93 — 39 = 45 litre 


Step 6: Calculation of Total Aggregate Quantity 


Total aggregate quantity required (volume in m?) 
= 1 — {(120/2.96 x 1 000) + (280/2.25 x 1 000) + 
(45/1 x 1000) + (145/1.55 x 1 000) + (39/1.29 x 1 000); 
= 1 — 0.041 — 0.124 — 0.045 — 0.034 — 0.030 = 0.726 


(Assumed: sp. gr, GGBFS = 2.96, fly ash = 2.25, 
sodium sillicate gel = 1.55, sodium hydroxide solution 
= 1.29) 


Step 7: Selection of Percentage Fine Aggregate and 
Calculation of Fine Aggregate Quantity 


Taking fine aggregate as 38 percent of total aggregates 
by mass, calculate fine aggregate in kg as: 


Fine aggregate = 0.726 x 1 000 x 2.72 x 0.38 = 750 kg 


(Assumed fine aggregate specific gravity = 2.72, 


Fine aggregate percent say 38 percent) 


Step 8: Calculation of Coarse Aggregate 


a) Coarse aggregate = (1 — 0.38) x 2.73 x 1 000 x 
0.726 = 1230 kg (Assumed coarse aggregate 
specific gravity = 2.73) 

b) Coarse aggregate 20 mm = 0.6 x 1 230 kg = 
738 kg, coarse aggregate 10 mm = 0.4 x 1230 kg 
492 kg (assuming ratio of coarse aggregates 
20 mm : 10 mm is 60 : 40 by mass) 


IS 17452 : 2020 


6 CURING 


Curing method mainly depends upon the raw materials 
used and mix composition. Some of the curing methods 
may be thermal curing, water curing and curing with 
curing compounds. Curing method may be decided with 
a view to achieving the requisite concrete properties. 
However, it is observed that for low calcium system, 
thermal curing may be more suitable and for high 
calcium system, air/water curing may be preferred. Care 
should be taken against leaching of alkali activators. 


7 SAFETY 


Safety precautions are specially important during 
handling of chemicals, batching, mixing, production 
and placement operations of alkali activated concrete. 
Some of the safety guidelines given below should be 
followed: 


a) The pesonnel at site who are handling the 
activators and involved in concrete production 
should be trained enough to do so and the 
precautions while handling such materials 
should be explained before starting the activity. 


b) Raw materials should be procured only with 
material safety data sheets and all instructions 
should be strictly followed . 

Manufacturer's recommendations for raw 
materials should be followed for storage of 
materials. 


Cc 


wa 


d) 


e 


wm 


g) 


h) 


No operations should be allowed, including 
handling and storage of materials, mixing, 
production and placement operations without 
proper personal protective equipment 
including gloves, masks, safety shoes and eye 
protectors. 


Extra precautions are required while mixing 
of chemicals in water. The containers in 
which chemicals are mixed should be able 
to withstand high temperatures as sodium 
hydroxide solution can easily reach 70 to 80° C 
within minutes of mixing. 


The solutions should be mixed in containers 
with lid to arrest fumes rising out of the 
solution. 


The mixing of alkali activated concrete 
should only be done through mechanical 
mixers. Site batching and mixing through 
manual mixing shall not be done. Proper 
arrangement such as additional dispensers 
for dispensing chemicals should be installed 
in the batching plant to avoid direct handling 
and measuring error. Due care should be taken 
while filling the activator dispensers . 

As the chemicals are of corrosive nature, it 
is advisable to have anti-corrosive lining on 
storage containers and mixers.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
